header: How the institute reads the Anbach
bodytext:
Every 15 minutes, each of the 46 stations along the Anbach records water level, temperature, dissolved oxygen and turbidity. Compared with 12 years of earlier data, a single reading shows whether the gravel beds below the weir are silting up again.

What a station measures

The standard mast carries four sensors and a logger. Level and temperature are measured continuously. Oxygen and turbidity are calibrated by hand twice a year, because a drifting oxygen probe is worse than none.

  • Water level, to the centimetre
  • Temperature at two depths
  • Dissolved oxygen
  • Turbidity, as a measure of suspended sediment

Why we also publish the raw data

We publish the raw series next to the checked one. Anyone checking a flood peak against our report can see which values we removed, and why. The data licence only asks you to credit the series.
